verdicts.claim: Every genesis card, written as a PNG with the real art engine and read back, returns exactly its dossier (canonical bytes equal), with its facts.
Every genesis card written twice is byte-identical: the same life makes the same card.

On every tenth genesis card, each of 12 forgeries — a face pixel flipped, a byte after the dossier, another card’s face, a changed owner, a changed serial, a changed genome byte, a re-wrapped dossier, a cut-short file, a damaged chunk, the wrong size, an event signed by a stranger, the magic removed — is refused, every one.
verdicts.saw: a face pixel flipped 100/100; a byte after the dossier 100/100; another card’s face 100/100; a changed owner 100/100; a changed serial 100/100; a changed genome byte 100/100; a re-wrapped dossier 100/100; a cut-short file 100/100; a damaged chunk 100/100; the wrong size 100/100; an event signed by a stranger 100/100; the magic removed 100/100

verdicts.claim: Reading a card touches no network: every read on the sampled cards runs with the network trapped and never reaches for it.
verdicts.saw: 100 of 100 read with the network trapped; 0 reached for it

verdicts.claim: A level signed into a card by its own owner with made-up numbers still reads (a card proves what it is), and is refused by the registry, which re-runs every level before recording it — on every sampled card.
verdicts.saw: 100 of 100 faked cards read; 100 refused by the registry

verdicts.claim: The median time to read and fully check a card (CRCs, seals, signatures, redrawn face) is at most 250 ms on the measuring machine.
verdicts.saw: median 84 ms, 90th percentile 100 ms (win32 x64 node v25.7.0)
